clue.text: In light rain returns to Teignmouth and finds ancient ammunition factory

indicators.note: the word In tells us the following piece sits inside the light rain

parts.note: a shower is a brief fall of light rain

indicators.note: returns says the little word to and its partner letter are read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
the mouth, or opening, of the Teign is its first letter T

explanation.surface: A visitor to a Devon seaside town in drizzle stumbles on an old munitions works.
explanation.walkthrough: Teignmouth is a seaside town in Devon; its 'mouth' is read as the opening letter of the River Teign. The little reversed piece reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead shot was once made by dropping molten metal down a tall tower into water, so such a tower was a factory for musket balls.

clue.text: Meet a famous mountaineer

definitions.meaning: a meet is a gathering of riders and hounds for a chase
John ... led the 1953 British Everest expedition

explanation.definitionFit: A fox-hunting gathering is called a meet, and Lord Hunt was the leader of the first successful Everest ascent.

clue.text: Dishonest contortionist?

parts.note: read as a performer who bends the body, yet also a cheat who bends the truth

explanation.definitionFit: A swindler is called a twister, and someone who bends their limbs into knots could literally be described the same way.

clue.text: Church music is playing piece of mediaeval music

parts.note: the organ is the instrument that supplies music in church
something that is on is running or playing

explanation.surface: A hymn sounds out in church while an old plainsong piece is performed.
explanation.definitionFit: Early polyphony in which voices were added to plainchant is known by this name, a variant of organum.

clue.text: Draw back about ten only to be way out

indicators.note: about means the reversed draw goes round the Roman ten
back says the word for a level score is read backwards

parts.note: a tie is a draw in a match
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Someone pulls back from a figure of ten only to find themselves far off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TIE into EIT; 'about' wraps that round X.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is a door or route by which people leave a building.

clue.text: Nevertheless let's resort to cunning without due consideration

parts.note: though can mean nevertheless, as in 'he came, though'

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort, rearranging these four letters

parts.note: sly means cunning or crafty

explanation.surface: Despite everything, someone decides to fall back on trickery, acting rashly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' is read as re-sort: LETS rearranged gives TLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting heedlessly means acting carelessly, with no regard for consequences.

clue.text: Starting off too early for rousing game with the appropriate weapon

parts.note: beaters at a shoot rouse game birds by beating the undergrowth
taken as written
a gun is the weapon used at a shoot

explanation.surface: Shooting talk: setting off prematurely to flush the birds with the right firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: On a British game shoot, beaters drive pheasants towards the guns.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means acting too soon, like a runner who leaves before the starting pistol.

clue.text: Unsettled periods may be the cause of jet lag

definitions.text: may be the cause of jet lag
definitions.meaning: flying across zones moves the clock forward or back, upsetting the body

explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent eras are said to be times that are shifting, and crossing time zones shifts the clock, causing travel fatigue.

clue.text: Frank beaten in debate

definitions.meaning: frank means candid and direct in speech
read as ..., outdone by a better speaker

explanation.definitionFit: A candid person speaks bluntly, and someone outclassed by a better orator has been out-talked.

clue.text: Naturally they can't reach as far-as artillery?

definitions.text: Naturally they can't reach as far-as artillery?

parts.words: Naturally they can't reach as far-as artillery?
parts.note: seems to describe short limbs, but also names light firearms whose range is less than big guns

explanation.definitionFit: Pistols and rifles are handheld weapons with a shorter range than cannon, and little limbs naturally reach less far.

clue.text: Army heading off Taurus still means bull

indicators.note: heading off means the army letters are removed from the front of the star sign

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army

explanation.surface: Troops turn away from the constellation, which still signifies a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: Taurus, the star sign, means bull in Latin; removing TA from its start leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The urus is the extinct wild ox, also called the aurochs, the ancestor of domestic cattle.

clue.text: Make amends an hour after midday

definitions.meaning: to make up for a wrong
read as ..., one o'clock in the afternoon

explanation.definitionFit: To expiate a sin is to make reparation, and one o'clock is sixty minutes past noon.

clue.text: It has me turning over part of the newspaper

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: turning over means the little word me is flipped backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone flips through a paper and finds themselves featured in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of the newspaper' could mean a section, but here it is a single piece of news.
explanation.definitionFit: A single news story or article in a paper is called an item.

clue.text: Fish harpoon

definitions.meaning: a flatfish, such as a flounder
the barbed head of a harpoon or anchor arm

explanation.definitionFit: The flounder is also known by this name, and the barb on a harpoon or anchor carries the same name.

clue.text: Is it clever to be well-groomed?

explanation.definitionFit: Smart describes both a sharp intellect and a neat, stylish appearance.

clue.text: He studies one short chapter in sunny surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the sunny word encloses the shortened chapter

parts.note: solar means relating to the sun
CH is the short form of chapter

explanation.surface: A student reads one brief section of a book while sitting out in the sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: A learned person or student devoted to academic study is a scholar.

clue.text: Lion man dismembered in name only

indicators.note: dismembered means the letters of the two words are torn apart and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gruesome scene of a lion tearing a man apart, though only nominally.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nominal exists by title alone, without real substance.

clue.text: Waterproof coat to protect against sunburn?

definitions.meaning: a coat of oiled cloth worn by sailors
read as oil on the skin, as with sun lotion

explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman's slicker is made of oiled cloth, and rubbing oil on one's body guards against the sun.

clue.text: Denied revolver being used in necessity

indicators.note: being used in means the gun is placed inside the word for necessity

parts.note: need means necessity
gat is slang for a gun or revolver

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to admit a handgun was used out of sheer necessity.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate a claim is to deny or nullify it.

clue.text: Something about a sapper with an army church cap

indicators.note: about means the small piece goes round the soldier's letters

parts.note: a bit is a small something
RE, the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are sappers
TA is the Territorial Army

explanation.surface: A tale of an engineer soldier and a chaplain wearing a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square cap with ridges worn by Catholic clergy.

clue.text: Can't see Jenny in bed

indicators.note: in means the singer's surname goes inside the bed

parts.note: taken as written
Jenny Lind was the Swedish soprano known as the Swedish Nightingale

explanation.surface: A woman called Jenny lies in bed unable to see.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenny Lind was a famous 19th-century Swedish opera singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deprived of sight has been rendered sightless.

clue.text: Blend of teas from the Orient

indicators.note: a blend mixes things, so the four letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A mixture of teas imported from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is an old name for Asia, the region to the sunrise side of Europe.

clue.text: A profit, and not for the first time

parts.note: a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: A businessman makes money yet once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something a second or further occasion means repeating it once more.

clue.text: Germany lacks any means of biological warfare

indicators.note: lacks means the country name is missing these three letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A country is said to have no biological weapons programme at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A microbe or bacterium can be used as an agent in biological weapons.

clue.text: Scratch starter gets the urge

definitions.meaning: what sets off scratching: an irritation of the skin
a restless longing to do something

explanation.definitionFit: A skin irritation prompts scratching, and a strong desire is also an irritation, as in itching to go.

clue.text: Did she find Siam small change from India?

definitions.meaning: ... Leonowens was governess at the Siamese court, as in ... and the King of Siam
a former Indian coin worth a sixteenth of a rupee

explanation.definitionFit: Anna Leonowens taught at the court in Bangkok, and an anna was a small former Indian coin.

clue.text: Commonplace mix up with Latin studio

indicators.note: mix means the letters that follow are shuffled together into a new word

explanation.surface: Someone muddles up an ordinary arrangement involving an Italian art studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix' rearranges UP and LATINSTUDIO together; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal, trite remarks are platitudes, so speech full of them is unoriginal.

clue.text: Maybe stained pine no honest tradesman would be involved in

definitions.text: no honest tradesman would be involved in

parts.note: stained wood may be darkened, shaded, so shady
deal is softwood timber such as pine or fir

explanation.surface: Darkened pine boards are something a decent carpenter would never touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stained' looks like a woodwork term, and deal is indeed pine timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A dishonest transaction or crooked bargain is something a reputable trader avoids.
